name: Dermalogen / Autologen

lead: Autologen and Dermalogen are injectable dermal fillers made from human collagen, used to add volume to the lips and soften lines. Autologen is processed from the patient's own skin; Dermalogen is made from donor tissue. The filling is visible after injection.

A 2000 article on facial soft-tissue augmentation described them as physiologic and consistent with many qualities of an ideal dermal filler. A 2004 review classed them as autograft and homograft fillers respectively. Wikipedia says Autologen is absorbed quickly, so results are very temporary, and that some studies suggest Dermalogen lasts somewhat longer than standard collagen.

paras: Human collagen is processed and injected into the skin by a clinician, where it adds volume until the body gradually absorbs it. Results are described as short-to-moderate in duration, so use is repeated if people want to keep the look.
The sources reviewed describe low immune risk because the material is human-derived, with no allergy risk reported for Autologen, and results are temporary. No detailed safety trials were found.

angle.text: Injectable collagen made from the patient's own skin (Autologen) or donor tissue (Dermalogen) adds volume to the lips and softens lines. The filling is visible after injection and is gradually absorbed. Sources describe short-to-moderate persistence and low allergy risk.

lead: Autologen and Dermalogen are injectable dermal fillers consisting of human tissue collagen matrix. Autologen is derived from the patient's own skin, and Dermalogen from donor (allogeneic) tissue [1][2].

A 2000 article in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery described dermal augmentation with these matrices as physiologic and as appearing ultimately safe and effective, with many qualities of an ideal filler [1]. A 2004 review of injectables placed Autologen among autografts and Dermalogen among homografts, noting that no perfect filler exists [2].

Wikipedia's lip augmentation article says Autologen has no allergy risk but is absorbed rapidly, and that Dermalogen may last slightly longer than standard collagen, though that claim is marked as needing a citation [3].
infobox: Described as short; Dermalogen possibly longer than bovine collagen [3]

paras: These products belong to the family of collagen fillers that replaced or followed bovine collagen, which required allergy testing [3]. The human-derived versions avoid that requirement in Wikipedia's account [3].

No controlled trials were found. A 2000 narrative article in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery discusses Autologen and Dermalogen among agents for facial soft-tissue augmentation, concluding they appear safe and effective in its authors' view [1]; a 2004 review in Facial Plastic Surgery compares injectable categories but is a narrative overview [2]. Other items found under these names concern knee cartilage and vocal fold collagen and are not about these products.
